segment: Substation transformers 10-60 MVA (to ~100), 69-138 kV primaries (HTS 8504.23.0040/0041), via an acquired plant or a brownfield line with a test bay
why:
This is where EO coverage, scarcity and pricing power overlap:
• EO 14421 reaches equipment at ≥69 kV with no MVA floor.
• Municipal quotes run ~130 weeks.
• Power makers show price-led margin gains.
• Several incumbent additions in this band are late or smaller than announced (Gallman relocation, Rincon slip, Muscle Shoals unverified, Niagara pre-construction).
• Korean units below 60 MVA pay no antidumping duty, though.

The 'high' rating applies only to a buyer with a qualified plant or a ~$100-140M brownfield line with a test bay. As greenfield it is low. Utility unit demand is not counted, and Howard (250 MVA/345 kV, end-2026), Prolec Goldsboro (+200 units, end-2027) and Gallman (2029) compete directly.

segment: 3-phase pad-mount and unit substations, ~0.5-5 MVA (HTS 8504.22; dry >500 kVA in 8504.34)
why:
The fastest product to build: ~12-18 months in an existing building.

For it:
• 25% tariff shelter against imports.
• Data-center pull of 460-890 units per GW.
• Prices of ~$28-32/kVA at 1.5-2 MVA.
• New-unit quotes were still 40-50 weeks in early 2026.

Against it:
• EO 14421 excludes local distribution.
• Chinese-owned US plants (JST/Jinpan, Eaglerise) and Korean makers already compete on price.
• Stated 2027 additions roughly match data-center pull in ERCOT and PJM.

Use it as the volume base and phase-1 product, not the thesis. Upside if DOE treats generating-station MV step-ups (solar/BESS) as covered.

Buyers pay for speed:
• Rebuilt pad-mounts sell at near-new $/kVA ($18-34/kVA) with 4-12 week delivery.
• Small municipal utilities are turning to remanufacturers.
• Emergency units carry a ~33% premium.

It also trains coil winders and builds utility relationships. But PE roll-ups (TJC/Sunbelt Solomon, IPS/Belyea, Voltaris) compete for targets, and no margin data was found.

segment: Small and mid GSUs (≤100 MVA) for industrial/aeroderivative turbines, hydro and BESS
why:
These come off the same factory capability as the 69-138 kV line, and GSU lead times are the longest in the market:
• Siemens booked 48 industrial turbines in one quarter.
• USACE plans a ~10-year hydro custom-transformer IDIQ.
• Snohomish is buying two 52.8 MVA GSUs.

Against that, GSUs are custom and need a proven test bay. Korean makers (LS Electric) are already shortlisted, and US unit counts by size are weak. Treat this as a phase-3 option.

segment: Large power / EHV >100 MVA incl. 765 kV
why:
The tightest market, and the wrong one for a newcomer:
• 765 kV demand is under ~150 units over 2029-34.
• Plants cost $150-457M and qualification takes years.
• Shelter is 15% through 2027, with 0% antidumping for HD Hyundai.
• Incumbents are expanding (Hyosung, HD Hyundai, Siemens, Hitachi, PTT).
Lead times are the longest of any class, but the barriers are the same as large power. Large-frame turbine backlogs (GE Vernova, MHI) translate into LPT-class units for incumbents.

Loosening:
• Stock quotes of 6-13 weeks; Howard says most of its lines are under 20 weeks.
• Units sell for ~$3,000.
• Incumbents are entrenched (Howard, ERMCO, Eaton, Central Moloney).
• Korean makers sit on Austin Energy's contracts.
• Cores must be redesigned for the 2029 efficiency rule.

Shows the clearest softening at maker level:
• Hammond's backlog fell 6.9% QoQ, and Canadian pricing is competitive.
• Hammond's Mexico plants are ramping.
• 8504.34 above 500 kVA gets only 15% shelter until end-2027.

Cliffs strip is not available to newcomers, and imported strip reportedly pays 50%. Revisit if cores are confirmed at 50% duty, which would make domestic cutting more valuable, or if Cliffs opens merchant allocations after 2028.

Venture-funded and unproven at scale:
• Heron's 286k sq ft Morgan Hill plant targets late 2027, with a $26.4M CalCompetes award and an RWE pilot.

It is a medium-term substitution risk in data-center MV, not a fit for a conventional builder.
